description: Signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management and the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People’s Republic of China
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management, functioning under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism, has initiated a collaboration with the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People's Republic of China with the aim of establishing a policy framework for institutional cooperation in areas including academic exchange, professional training, collaborative research, faculty development and sharing of knowledge resources. A Memorandum of Understanding has been drafted, including the observations of the Attorney General as well to regularize the said cooperation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to sign the proposed Memorandum of Understanding between the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management and the Central Academy of Culture and Tourism Administration of the People's Republic of China, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for empowering people affected by the disaster
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025 12 05, granted approval for the implementation of the programme for empowering those affected by the disaster to restore the livelihood that was disrupted due to the sudden disaster situation caused by the Cyclone Ditwah. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to pursue action as follows to address the issues identified while reviewing the progress of the empowerment programme held in several Districts that were most affected by the said sudden disaster situation, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	to issue necessary Circular instructions enabling to extend the monthly house rent allowance provided for a maximum period of 06 months to homeowners who lost their houses and do not own a house for residence, up to a maximum period of 09 months to temporarily settle in another place until they are able to construct their own houses.

* 	to issue Circulars and instructions regarding the removal of rocks, soil and debris accumulated on paddy lands and restore the said paddy lands to suitable condition for cultivation after obtaining the approval of relevant institutions as per an estimate approved for the same by the District Deputy Commissioner/Assistant Commissioner of Agrarian Development.

* 	to use the provisions allocated under the Landslide Mitigation Programme under the Ministry of Defence with priority to carry out landslide risk mitigation activities in locations where rock falls and earth slips have occurred or in areas prone to landslides, as recommended by the National Building Research Organization.

* 	to provide the necessary provisions appropriately through the provisions allocated for disaster relief and rehabilitation activities by the General Treasury.

description: Declaration of Elephant Corridors in Monaragala and Hambantota Districts to minimize human-elephant conflicts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Wild elephants live in about 2/3 of the country's land area, and the rapid blockage of wild elephant habitats and migration routes due to various development projects and human activities has directly affected the escalation of elephant-human conflicts. It has been identified that the protection of wild elephant habitats and migration routes should be done urgently to minimize such conflicts to some extent. The Department of Wildlife Conservation, in collaboration with the relevant Divisional Secretaries, stakeholder institutions and organizations, is currently identifying the migration routes of wild elephants. Under the programme to identify wild elephant migration routes in the Monaragala District, the wild elephant migration route from Handapanagala to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara has been identified, and the approval for the same has also been received from the Monaragala District Coordination Committee. The elephant migration route from Lunugamvehera National Park in Zone VI of the Yala National Park to Udawalawe National Park was declared as the Wetahira Kanda Wildlife Sanctuary in the year 2002. 05 plots of land with land permits have been identified in the relevant area, and these lands have not been developed yet. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take the following steps, was approved by the Cabinet:

* 	To declare the elephant migration route from Handapanagala in the Monaragala District to the Yala National Park via the Menik River in Demodara as a sanctuary under the provisions of the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance.

*	To re-declare the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve as a 'Forest Gateway' by providing alternative lands at a suitable location outside the wildlife reserve, instead of 05 plots of land with land permits located within the Watahira Kanda Nature Reserve Area.

*	To acquire the plots of land including the buildings constructed blocking the Koholankala Elephant corridor in the Hambantota District by paying compensation and declare the area belonging to the Hambantota Wild Elephant Management Reserve as a sanctuary.

description: Submission of the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No.04 of 2026 to Parliament for approval
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Hydrochlorofluorocarbons, chemical compound widely used in refrigerators and air conditioning units, are being phased out globally under the Montreal Protocol due to their ozone-depletion and high global warming potential. Accordingly, Sri Lanka is also committed to phase out this series of chemicals by 2030. Accordingly, the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No.04 of 2026 under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act, No.1 of 1969 has been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification dated 2026 05 07, to ban the importation of equipment and accessories operating exclusively with hydrochlorofluorocarbons with effect from 06-06-2026 and to prohibit the import of compressors operating exclusively with hydrochlorofluorocarbons used as a component of the refrigeration system for equipment and accessories with effect from 01-01-2028. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit the said Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Small Towns and Rural Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Access to safe drinking water has yet to be fully realized for the people residing in small towns and rural areas of Sri Lanka, which remains a major challenge affecting the social and economic development of the country. It has been planned to implement a programme to provide clean drinking water to about 600,000 families living in semi-urban and rural areas through 300 projects covering 50 small towns and rural areas, redressing the said situation.  The projects aim to establish safe, reliable and sustainable drinking water supply systems, and it is expected to treat the water using modern treatment technologies including chlorination and filtration systems in accordance with national and international drinking water standards. Accordingly, taking into consideration a proposal submitted by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply, the Cabinet granted its approval for the proposed programme to be implemented by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board and the Department of National Community Water Supply during the period 2027-2029 by conducting a feasibility study on the said programme and including it in the Public Investment Programme based on its results.

description: Awarding the procurement for the supply of Lubricating Oil for Sapugaskanda Power Station for a period of 2026/27
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026 02 09 to implement the procurement for the supply of lubricating oil to Plant A and Plant B of the Sapugaskanda Power Station for the period of 2026/27. Accordingly, bids have been invited following the National Competitive Procurement Methodology, and 03 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the relevant procurements as follows, based on the recommendations made by the High Level Procurement Committee, after evaluating the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet:
*	Awarding the contract for the supply of 316,000 liters of lubricating oil to Plant A of the Sapugaskanda Power Station to Lanka IOC PLC, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.392.47 million (inclusive of VAT).

* 	Awarding the contract for the supply of 304,000 liters of lubricating oil to Plant B of the Sapugaskanda Power Station to Chevron Lubricants Lanka PLC, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of Rs.434.86 million (inclusive of VAT).

description: Awarding the Contract for the Construction of Lot A of the Mullikulam Wind Power Transmission Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025 02 03 to implement the Mullikulam Wind Power Transmission Project. The project consists of two projects, namely Lot A and Lot B and the contract for the construction of Lot B of the project has been awarded by now. Bids have been invited following the International Competitive Procurement Methodology for the construction of Lot A, which includes the incomer side of the Mullikulam 220/33 kV Collector Grid Substation and the Construction of 02 Nos. of 220 kV Line Bays at the said Grid Substation. 04 bids have been received for the same. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the said contract to RS Infraprojects (Pvt) Ltd. of India, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a sum of US$ 6.04 million and Sri Lankan Rupees 499.66 million (excluding VAT) based on the recommendation submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee after evaluating the said bids, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Project for the construction of the Amaradeva Aesthetic and Research Centre (Amaradeva Asapuwa)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The construction of the Amaradeva Aesthetics and Research Centre (Amaradeva Asapuwa) was initiated by the then Ministry of Mass Media as a special budget proposal presented in the year 2017, in grateful recognition of the invaluable national contribution rendered by Dr. Pandit Amaradeva to the field of music in Sri Lanka. Although about 09 years have elapsed since the construction work began, it has not been completed yet. Although the General Treasury has provided a provision of Rs.226.18 million in the year 2025 to complete the relevant construction work and purchase essential office equipment, only Rs.141.54 million of the said provisions has been spent in the year 2025. The proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to secure provisions of Rs.113.17 million to complete all work of the project within this year, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of 25 Towns under the 'Mithuru Purawara Programme'
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - According to the 2026 Budget Proposals, more attention has been placed on urban development, and a development programme titled 'Mithuru Purawara' has been proposed to be implemented thereunder. The said programme, which is centered on the objective of 'development of small towns for the convenience and well-being of the public and local communities', is expected to identify one essential development activity in each of 25 selected towns in the island and complete it during the year 2026. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to allocate an estimated amount of Rs. 581 million under the 'Clean Sri Lanka' programme for the implementation of the projects identified in 23 towns identified for implementation in the initial phase of the 'Mithuru Purawara' programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation and Improvement of the Road Lighting System of the Colombo - Katunayake Expressway, Including the Kerawalapitiya Interchange
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The road lighting system on the Colombo-Katunayake Expressway, including the Kerawalapitiya Interchange, has suffered significant damage due to persistent vandalism and theft, mainly carried out by drug addicts, and approximately 85% of the lighting system is currently non-functional. Therefore, considering the cost of lighting the entire length of the expressway, it has been planned to light only the Peliyagoda, Kerawalapitiya, Seeduwa and Ja-Ela interchanges as well as the freeway sections from the New Kelani Bridge to the Peliyagoda Fish Market and from Seeduwa to the Bandaranaike International Airport in the first phase. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to have the rehabilitation and improvement of the lighting system of those road sections carried out in two packages at an estimated cost of Rs.1,098.50 million, through contractors selected following the National Competitive Procurement Methodology, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Projects identified under the Development of 10 Cities Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development has been allocated Rs.1,300 million through the 2026 budget to redevelop the attractive cities identified in Sri Lanka as model cities, highlighting their heritage and identity, and to popularize them among local and foreign tourists through city branding. Accordingly, the said project is expected to be implemented based on a study conducted by a suitable consultancy firm based on the concept of City Branding, highlighting the identity and uniqueness of the cities of Anuradhapura, Kataragama, Colombo and Kandy. For the purpose, it is estimated that about Rs.325 million will be spent for the year 2026.

Also, the 2026 budget has proposed to implement the 10 Cities Development Programme as well with the aim of promoting a systematic, prioritized and data driven approach in the field of urban development. Under the said programme, 217 prioritized projects identified in the cities of Jaffna, Matale, Hatton, Batticaloa, Chilaw, Thambuttegama, Vavuniya, Eheliyagoda, Badulla and Matara have been planned to be implemented. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to expeditiously implement the projects identified under the 10 Cities Development Programme for the year 2026, using a total of Rs.1,475 million, comprising the remaining Rs.975 million of the provisions allocated for the budget 2026 for the City Branding Project and including the Rs.500 million allocated for the development of Hatton and Matale cities, since development of those cities are also covered under this programme, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Digitalization of the plans of 3.5 million land plots available in hard copy form at the Survey Department of Sri Lanka and their integration into the Land Information System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It is estimated that there are about 16 million plots of land in Sri Lanka. Of these, about 6 million plots of land have been surveyed so far, and the information on about 2.5 million of them is available in digitized format. The data has been entered into a Land Information System and published on the website of the Survey Department of Sri Lanka. With the aim of improving land management efficiency and decision-making capacity by providing access to accurate and verifiable land information to government institutions, stakeholders and the public, a project has been planned to digitize the information on the remaining 3.5 million plots of land in hard copy form, which have been surveyed since 1800, and enter them into the Land Information System. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation for the implementation of the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Updated Guidelines for the Sri Lanka National Green Reporting System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - With the aim of promoting sustainable performance in the manufacturing and service sectors, the 'National Green Reporting System' was established in the year 2012 with the approval of the Cabinet. For the purpose, the third generation standards of 2011 of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), which is an international sustainable reporting framework, were adopted as the basis. Since the standards of the International Sustainable Reporting Framework have been updated by 2025 and taking into account the current global trends such as climate change, Sustainable Development Goals and obligations related to the Paris Agreement, the need to revise the National Green Reporting System has been identified. Accordingly, measures have been taken to update the International Sustainable Reporting Guidelines, consisting of a total of 76 indicators, including 31 environmental indicators, 30 social indicators and 15 governance indicators. Similarly, 05 reporting levels have been introduced for institutions that agree to follow the National Green Reporting System. Measures have also been taken to re-constitute the National Green Reporting Steering Committee with 24 members, including the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka and the Sustainable Development Council of Sri Lanka. Accordingly, Cabinet decided to grant its concurrence to implement the updated Sri Lanka National Green Reporting System and the Guidelines referred to above, submitted by the Minister of Environment for the attention of the Cabinet.

description: Revised National Oil and Hazardous and Noxious Substance Spill Contingency Plan and its Digital Platform
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that with over 400 vessels transiting daily in the East-West maritime routes located adjacent to Sri Lanka and over 5000 ships calling at Sri Lankan ports annually, expansion of existing ports, growth in oil-related activities and the impact of global climate change, there is a risk of oil and hazardous and noxious substances spilling in the Sri Lankan waters in the future, thereby causing a marine environmental damage. As per the provisions of the Marine Pollution Prevention Act, No.35 of 2008, it is a duty of the Marine Environment Protection Authority to formulate and implement a scheme to prevent such pollution in the Sri Lankan waters. Accordingly, the National Oil Spill Contingency Plan, previously prepared as per the said provisions upon the approval of the Cabinet, has been revised, having included response mechanisms for Hazardous and Noxious Substances. Similarly, the first phase of the Digital Platform of the said National Plan has also been prepared. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to implement the proposed National Plan on an instance of an Oil and Hazardous & Noxious Substance Spill Contingency, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Waste Management within the Coastal Zone including the Fishery Harbours in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The improper disposal of waste, including large quantities of waste, plastic discharged from the inland areas of the country into the ocean through rivers and waterways, together with the improper disposal of large quantities of fibreglass waste near fishery harbours, ferries and anchorage points, which has led to numerous health, social and environmental problems, has placed the sensitive ecosystems spread across the coastal zone of Sri Lanka under threat. Although there are several number of institutions for solid waste management in the coastal zone of the island, as a solution to the problem of lack of proper coordination between these institutions, the Marine Environment Protection Authority has established the National Committee for Waste Management in Coastal areas including fishery harbours and 84 regional committees by involving Local Government institutions in coastal districts. Accordingly, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take the following steps regarding waste management within the coastal zone:

*	To implement the 'Proposal for Waste Management in Coastal Zone and Fishery Harbours' prepared by the Marine Environment Protection Authority in collaboration with the institutions belonging to the National Committee and other stakeholder institutions.

* 	To use the mobile app developed to more efficiently fulfil the responsibilities included in the proposal.

* 	To take necessary action to amend the Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Act, No.2 of 1996 and the Marine Pollution Prevention Act, No.35 of 2008 to introduce and implement the principle of 'Extended Producer Responsibility' to assign responsibilities for the proper disposal of fiberglass waste.

description: Construction of the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit on the Fourth Floor at the new Paediatric Ward Complex at the Teaching Hospital - Ratnapura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ratnapura Teaching Hospital, the main tertiary healthcare provider in the Sabaragamuwa Province, provides a wide range of medical services and, as it is currently affiliated to the University of Sabaragamuwa, also contributes to advancing medical education and research. As per the approval given at the Cabinet meeting held on 2016-07-26, a Memorandum of Understanding has been signed with local donors who have offered to provide financial assistance for the construction of a five-storied building for the Paediatric Ward Complex of the said hospital and accordingly, construction work has been carried out up to the third floor of the said building. Local donors have again come forward to provide financial assistance for the construction of the fourth floor of the new ward complex to establish the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit. The recommendation of the Department of National Planning has also been received for the relevant project. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Health and Mass Media and the relevant donors to implement the project to construct the 'Paediatric Intensive Care Unit' on the fourth floor of the new Paediatric Ward Complex at the Teaching Hospital, Ratnapura, by obtaining funding contributions of Rs.64.15 million, which is the total estimated cost of the project, from local donors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Enhancing community access through Arogya Wellness Centres
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka's health needs are rapidly changing due to the ongoing demographic and epidemiological transitions, resulting in a triple burden of non communicable diseases, communicable diseases and injuries. Sri Lanka’s primary care delivery, which is divided between the public and private sectors, predominantly operates on a model that focuses mainly on treating acute conditions. Although, the Universal Health Coverage Service Index of Sri Lanka, remains lower than expected, it is above the regional average. Accordingly, with the objective of increasing disease control and free healthcare access, the Ministry of Health and Mass Media has planned to establish 'Arogya Health and Wellness Centres' in line with the vision of 'A Thriving Nation-A Beautiful Life'. As decided at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-09-15 and also taking into account the recommendations made by the Committee appointed to submit recommendations for the more effective and efficient implementation of the proposed project to increase community access through Arogya Health and Wellness Centers, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Labour and the Acting Minister if Health and Mass Media to establish 1,000 Arogya Health and Wellness Centers during the period 2026-2028 in a phased out manner thereby increasing the total number of primary care institutions, including the existing regional hospitals and primary medical care units, to 2,000 and to provide the necessary human and physical resources for the said centers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Developing an appropriate programme to secure the unsafe and high risk areas on roads that are not under the purview of the National Road System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-06-01 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The number of lives lost and property damages reported due to road accidents in Sri Lanka is increasing, and it has been observed that a significant number of these accidents occur on rural and regional roads that do not fall under the national road system. However, it has been identified that this situation continues due to the lack of adequate financial provisions in the existing institutional structures at the regional level to eliminate those dangerous situations and ensure road safety. Therefore, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to utilize the provisions allocated to the Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development under Road Safety and Traffic Management in the National Budget for the year 2026 for the said road development work, by identifying relevant proposals at the district level to take steps such as installing road signs, constructing security guard rails, marking road signs, installing speed limit barriers, etc. to make unsafe and risky places in the road system which do not fall under the national road system, safe, having obtained the views and proposals of the Provincial Councils as well.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of the Department of Management Services
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A committee has been appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to make recommendations regarding the appointment of a suitable officer to the Post of Director General of the Department of Management Services, which fell vacant at present following the appointment of Mr. Wimal S.K. Liyanagama, the former Director General of the Department of Management Services, as the Director General of Customs. Based on the recommendations made by the said Committee, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to appoint Mrs. M.K.D.N. Madampe, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving in a Post of Additional Director General of the Department of Management Services, to the post of Director General of the Department of Management Services with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Promotion of Export Agriculture Act, No.46 of 1992
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Legal provisions have been made by the Promotion of Export Agriculture Act, No.46 of 1992, to regulate and promote the export agriculture sector in the country. Taking into account the periodic administrative changes and the changes in the sector, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meetings held on 2023-09-04 and 2025-08-11 to amend the said Act, which has not been updated in over 30 years. The proposed amendments are expected to revise the designations of the Head of Department of Export Agriculture and other officers and to provide a clearer definition of 'export agricultural crop'. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to publish the Promotion of Export Agriculture (Amendment) Bill, which has been prepared in all three languages by the Legal Draftsman to amend the Promotion of Export Agriculture Act, No.46 of 1992, in the Government Gazette and thereafter submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Money or Value Transfer Service Providers Regulations No.1 of 2025, for approval of Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In order to ensure compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering/Countering the Financing Terrorism, Money or Value Transfer Service Providers Regulations No.1 of 2024 have been published under the provisions of Payment and Settlement Systems Act, No.28 of 2005. Accordingly, only the companies registered under the provisions of the Companies Act, No.7 of 2007, other than a company limited by guarantee, an offshore company or a foreign company, are eligible to obtain a certificate of registration under the said Regulations. However, it has been observed that foreign money or value transfer service providers are engaged in providing their services through their agents in Sri Lanka and such institutions are unable to obtain a certificate of registration from the Central Bank of Sri Lanka as per the regulations currently in force. Accordingly, the Money or Value Transfer Service Providers Regulations No.1 of 2025 has been published by the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2468/06 dated 2025-12-23, amending the Money or Value Transfer Service Providers Regulations No.1 of 2024, so that legal provisions would be provided for foreign money or value transfer service providers as well to obtain a registration certificate. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit the said Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Selling of Paddy Stocks belonging to the Paddy Marketing Board
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Paddy Marketing Board has stored approximately 115,000 metric tons of paddy purchased from farmers in the Board's warehouses, and it has been planned to retain a sufficient buffer stock from that paddy stock and sell the remaining portion in order to secure the necessary storage space and funds for the purchase of paddy from farmers in the upcoming Yala season. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to sell the said stock of paddy following the formal tender procedure, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the ‘Surakimu Lanka’ National Energy Security Mission
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The country's energy security has been challenged by factors such as dependence on fossil fuels for energy supply, unpredictable dry weather conditions, periodic disruptions in fuel supply due to geopolitical instability, and fluctuations in fuel prices in the international market. It has been recognized that the additional pressure on the national economy caused by the rising cost of fuel imports, together with all these factors, may further aggravate due to the irregular electricity consumption pattern of electricity consumers. Therefore, in order to properly manage the situation, it has been identified that behavioral changes of the general public are also essential to shift electricity consumption to periods with high renewable energy generation and to enhance the efficiency of energy consumption. In order to achieve the said objectives, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to implement a joint program called the 'Surakimu Lanka' National Energy Security Mission, led by the Presidential Secretariat, the Ministry of Energy, the Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority, the Clean Sri Lanka Secretariat, and with the participation of all Government Institutions, state corporations and statutory boards, the private sector and the general public.

description: Regulation of obtaining Manpower Services by State Enterprises and Protection of Labour Rights of Manpower Employees
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A trend of gradual increase in the number of workers hired on temporary basis from external manpower agencies by certain State Enterprises in Sri Lanka, instead of direct recruitment for their core operational activities, has been observed in recent times. Further, there appears to be instances where such workers have been employed in the same State Institution for a considerable period of time. As a result, a community of insecure employees has been created in such institutions, performing the same duties as permanent employees but do not have job security, statutory benefits and proper legal recognition. This is a deviation from the basic labor concept of equal pay for equal work. Since the rights and welfare of workers in the country should be ensured as per the Private Employment Agencies Convention of the International Labour Organization, the need to amend the existing legal provisions to regulate the employment of workers in manpower agencies and to protect their Labour rights has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to appoint a Committee comprising relevant officials and stakeholders to make recommendations on action to be taken and the amendment of the relevant laws and regulations in relation to manpower workers who have already been employed for a long time in the core business activities of State Enterprises, without causing prejudice for them, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into a Cooperation Agreement between Sri Lanka and Brazil to implement the ‘Sugarcane Project in Sri Lanka’
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Currently, about 90% of the country's sugar requirement is imported for which a significant amount of foreign exchange has to be incurred. The need for international technical cooperation has been identified to overcome the weaknesses and challenges faced by the local sugarcane sector. Considering this situation, the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, the Sugarcane Research Institute and the National Science Foundation of Sri Lanka, and the Brazilian Cooperation Agency and the Federal University of São Carlos of Brazil have jointly planned to implement a project called the 'Sugarcane Project in Sri Lanka'. The project is expected to leverage Brazil's expertise and experience as a global leader in sugarcane production to increase sugarcane yield and sugar production in Sri Lanka, improve the technical capacity of stakeholders through training and knowledge transfer, promote value addition and efficient use of by-products, and strengthen institutional capacity in the sugar production sector. The proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to implement the proposed project within a period of 36 months under the framework of the Technical Cooperation Agreement signed between the two countries in 2008, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Streamlining Inspection and Food Safety Procedures for Agricultural Food Products exported to Member Countries of the European Union
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Member countries of the European Union are coordinated under a common protection law regarding the permissible levels of pesticides/residues that may be present in food, known as Maximum Residue Levels. The Health and Food Safety Regulatory Authority, an Agency of the European Commission, has reported that the levels of agrochemical residues in certain fresh vegetables and fruits exported from Sri Lanka to the European Union member countries are significantly higher than Maximum Residue Levels by now. Therefore, the need to streamline adequate inspection and food safety procedures for Sri Lankan agricultural exports to prevent the future challenges of exporting agricultural products to the EU countries and other importing countries, has been identified. Accordingly, as an initial step, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to make it mandatory for all fresh vegetables and fruits to be exported at least only through farms, registered exporters and processing and packing plants that have been certified in accordance with the Sri Lankan Good Agricultural Practices (SLGAP) guidelines to ensure the quality of all fresh vegetables and fruits exported to the European Union.

description: Implementation of a project for Joint Genetic Resource Exchange and Development of High-vielding Salinity-tolerance Rice Varieties between                Sri Lanka and Vietnam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - With the aim of improving the productivity of rice cultivation, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Agriculture Cooperation was entered into between the Department of Agriculture of Sri Lanka and the Vietnamese Academy of Agricultural Sciences on 2025 05 05. Under the said Agreement, the two parties have agreed to implement a project titled ‘Development of High-vielding Salinity tolerance Rice Varieties Project between Sri Lanka and Vietnam’. The activities expected to be carried out under the said project include, exchange of germplasm of rice varieties, conducting joint breeding and hybridization programmes, evaluation and selection of advanced breeding lines under local conditions, establishment of field trials, training of research officers and knowledge exchange between the two countries. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to implement the proposed project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of Orders regarding the imposition of a surcharge of 50% on the Customs Import Duty levied on the importation of motor vehicles
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the prevailing war situation in the Middle East Region, all import costs have drastically increased and immediate measures must be taken to mitigate the possible adverse impact which creates on the national economy. Accordingly, with effect from 2026-05-16, without resorting to import restrictions on vehicles, it has been decided to impose 50% surcharge, to be effective only for 3 months, on the 30% customs import duty which is presently in force as per the provisions of the Customs Ordinance. The Order related thereto was issued by the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2488/56 dated 2026-05-15. Accordingly, the Order dated 2026-05-15 applies only to Letters of Credit opened for the importation of vehicles after 2026-05-16, and cause no impact on Letters of Credit opened for the importation of vehicles before that date.Similarly, by Gazette Notification No. 2488/69 dated 2026-05-17, an Order was issued to make the aforesaid surcharge applicable to vehicles, if any of the following particulars pertaining to Letters of Credit opened on or before 2026-05-15 for importation of vehicles, such as the number of vehicles, vehicle identification number, description of the vehicle, or technical specifications of the vehicle, are amended after 2026-05-15. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to submit relevant Orders to Parliament pertaining to the imposition of the above surcharges and the regularization of vehicle imports, in a manner that would not change the prices of vehicles currently being imported into Sri Lanka and would limit the importation of vehicles for the next 03 months, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Finalizing the identification and provision of relief to Officers of the Sri Lanka Police (including the Special Task Force) and the Tri-Forces who died or became disabled as a result of terrorist acts and related activities during the period of war
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-07-14 to appoint an Officials’ Committee to submit a Report containing recommendations on the measures to be taken to finalize the identification of and provision of relief to the Officers of the Sri Lanka Police (including the Special Task Force) and the Tri-Forces who died or became disabled as a result of terrorist acts and related activities during the period of war and to issue a General Circular in place of all the circulars issued from time to time to provide such relief. The said Committee has submitted its comprehensive Report containing observations and recommendations on 2026-05-12. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to issue circular instructions to grant relief to newly identified parties in the Tri-Forces, Sri Lanka Police and the Special Task Force as per the recommendations of the said Committee, without causing prejudice to the allowances being paid to the parties identified so far, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of District Secretary/Government Agent of the Administrative District of Ratnapura
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Post of District Secretary/Government Agent of Ratnapura is currently vacant as Mr. K.G.S. Nishantha, who served as the District Secretary/Government Agent of the Administrative District of Ratnapura, has been appointed to the Post of District Secretary/Government Agent of Kegalle with effect from 2026-04-27. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to appoint Mr. M.G. Lalith Ananda, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, to the post of District Secretary/Government Agent of Ratnapura with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Confirmation of Director Generals appointed on acting basis to the respective Posts
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval had been granted by the Cabinet decision dated 2020-01-02 to appoint Mr. M.K.C Senanayake, then a Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Planning Service to act full time in the Post of Director General of the Department of Fiscal Policy of the General Treasury and by the Cabinet decision dated 2024-12-09 to appoint Mr. P.M.K Hettiarachchi, then a Grade I Officer of the Sri Lanka Planning Service to act full time in the Post of Director General of the Department of Development Finance. In terms of the provisions of the Minute of the Sri Lanka Planning Service, the two Officers were promoted to the Special Grade of the Sri Lanka Planning Service by the Public Service Commission, on seniority basis, with effect from 2026-01-01. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to appoint Mr. M.K.C. Senanayake to the post of Director General of the Department of Fiscal Policy and Mr. P.M.K. Hettiarachchi to the post of Director General of the Department of Development Finance on permanent basis, with effect from 2026-01-01, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchase of 181 Motorcycles for the Island-Wide Range Offices and Beat Offices under the Department of Wildlife Conservation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-18 for the purchase of vehicles required for the Range Offices and Beat Offices of the Department of Wildlife Conservation, to be used for wild elephant management duties and other field duties. Accordingly, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-05-04 to award the relevant procurements for the purchase of 16 double cabs, 84 single cabs and 09 tractors. As a part of the said procurement, bids have been invited following the national competitive bidding procedure for the purchase of 181 motorcycles, and 04 bids have been received for the same. Following the evaluation of the said bids, based on the recommendations submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to award the relevant procurement to M/s David Pieris Motor Company, the substantially responsive lowest bidder, for a sum of Rs.91.26 million (excluding tax), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Purchasing of potatoes by the M/s Co-operative Wholesale Establishment directly from local farmers and sell them to consumers through M/s Lanka Sathosa Limited
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In order to protect local potato farmers with a fair market price, the Government has currently imposed a Special Commodity Levy of Rs.80/- per kg on the importation of potatoes. At the beginning of the harvesting season in the Nuwara Eliya and Badulla districts, middlemen and wholesale purchasers impose a farm gate price of Rs.200/- to Rs.220/- per kg of potato, and this price is likely to fluctuate with the increases in harvest volume in the coming days. Considering the need to protect and promote the local supply of essential food items in the country in the best and most appropriate manner, it has been planned to purchase potatoes directly from local potato farmers by M/s Co-operative Wholesale Establishment and sell the stocks to Lanka Sathosa Limited and release them to the market through the retail outlet network of Lanka Sathosa. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation and the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development to implement the proposed methodology, subject to purchasing a maximum of 1,000 kg of potato per farmer, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the National Media Project- ‘Healthy Food - Happy Life’
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet Meeting held on 2025-08-11 to implement the ‘Healthy Food - Happy Life’ Project by the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation in the year 2025, aiming to disseminate a food safety model for a healthy life, using the funds from the Clean Sri Lanka Programme. The Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to further implement the National Media Project- ‘Healthy Food - Happy Life’, which aims to ensure nutrition, disease prevention, mental well-being and nutritional security through clean food consumption from the early stages of child development to adulthood, by securing an amount of Rs.600 million from the provisions allocated under the ‘Clean Sri Lanka’ programme by the Sri Lanka Rupavahini Corporation in the years 2026, 2027 and 2028.

description: Implementation of the ‘Take Care-Surekemu Magathota’ Project during the period of 2026-2028
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet Meeting held on 2025-05-19 to implement the ‘Take Care-Surekemu Magathota’ Project by Independent Television Network Limited, covering 60 schools in the Island, using the funds from the ‘Clean Sri Lanka’ programme under the supervision of the Ministry of Health and Mass Media. As per the said approval, the project has been initiated in the year 2025, and has been planned to further implement during the period of 2026-2028. Accordingly, it is expected to implement the project in a broader manner by involving 100 schools in one year in coordination with the Traffic Management and Road Safety Division of the Sri Lanka Police and the Co-curricular Division of the Ministry of Education. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement the said project as proposed, in the years 2026, 2027 and 2028 by securing an amount of Rs.833 million from the provisions allocated under the 'Clean Sri Lanka' programme by Independent Television Network Limited under the supervision of the Ministry of Health and Mass Media, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Awarding the Contract for renewal of Microsoft Licenses at SriLankan Airlines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited under the Limited National Competitive Procurement Procedure to identify a suitable licensed service provider with the capacity to provide Microsoft licenses and related services to SriLankan Airlines Limited. Two (02) bids have been received for the same. Following the evaluation of the said bids, based on the recommendations submitted by the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation to award the relevant contract, to Crayon Software Lanka (Private) Limited., the substantially responsive lowest bidder, for a period of 02 years for a sum of US$ 1.816 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Improvement of Malabe-Kaduwela (B 263) Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited for the improvement of a road section of 5.56 km of the Malabe - Kaduwela Road (B 263) using the funds allocated under the Widening and Improvement Programme for National Highways, following the National Competitive Procurement Procedure, and eight (08) bids have been received for the same. Following the evaluation of the bids, based on the recommendation submitted by the High Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development to award the relevant contract to M/s Senarath Engineering (Pvt) Ltd, the substantially responsive lowest bidder, for a sum of Rs.819 million (VAT excluded), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Payment of compensation for damages caused to the paddy cultivation due to the construction of a salinity barrier across the Nilwala River in Matara
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025-07-07, has granted approval for the payment of compensation for the damages caused to paddy cultivation in the Matara District during the 7 consecutive seasons from the Yala season 2019 up to the Yala season 2022 due to the flood situation caused by the obstruction of the Nilwala River during the construction of the salinity barrier across the Nilwala River, getting the provisions allocated through the budget after conducting a proper assessment on the same. Accordingly, the amount of compensation has been calculated taking into account the cost and paddy price as per the compensation payment methods of the Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board, and an amount of Rs. 1,200 million has been allocated through the Budget 2026, for the payment of the relevant compensation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to pay compensation to the farmers who are eligible to receive compensation as follows, was approved by the Cabinet. description: Purchase of 15,000 MT of urea fertilizer required for the Yala Season 2026 by the Agrarian Services Committees of the Department of Agrarian Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although it has been estimated that 550,000 hectares of paddy land would be cultivated in the Yala Season 2026, it is currently estimated that the extent would be around 450,000-500,000 hectares. It has been calculated that about 75,000 MT of urea fertilizer will be required for this. Currently, 48,297.87 MT of fertilizer are being distributed by the Agrarian Service Committees having purchased from the existing fertilizer reserves in the country. In order to ensure the supply of fertilizer at a fixed price for the Yala Season 2026, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2026-04-06 to provide a 50 kg bag of urea fertilizer to farmers at Rs. 10,200/- through the Agrarian Services Centres. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to purchase 15,000 MT of urea fertilizer, which is further required for the Yala Season 2026, through the Agricultural Services Committees and supply the same to farmers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Non-implementation of the First Semi-Annual Water Tariff Revision for the year 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As per the water tariff formula approved at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-07-15, water sales unit cost has to be reviewed semi-annually, taking into account the changes in the major cost factors. According to the analysis carried out based on the Financial Statement of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board for the year 2025, it has been confirmed that it is possible to cover the entire operational cost through the existing water tariff. Therefore, the Board of Directors of the National Water Supply and Drainage Board has decided to maintain the water sales unit cost without increasing during the first 06 months of the year 2026. Accordingly, the Cabinet has granted its concurrence to the proposal submitted by the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to maintain the current water tariff without revision during the first 06 months of the year 2026.

description: Formulation of a Space Policy for Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Space technology and its applications have become indispensable components of national development, yielding substantial benefits across critical sectors such as disaster management, communication, defence, environmental monitoring and economic innovation. Taking into account the increasing strategic significance of space technologies, the need of having a unified national framework for the same has been identified. Therefore, the Ministry of Science and Technology has planned to develop a National Space Policy. The proposed Policy will streamline and facilitate international cooperation, enhance Sri Lanka's effectiveness in global space governance mechanisms, and ensure that all national space activities are conducted in accordance with international obligations, treaties and standards. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to appoint an Expert Committee with specialized technical knowledge to formulate the National Space Policy, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulation of a National Intellectual Property Policy for Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Currently, a comprehensive legal framework for the protection of intellectual property is provided under the Intellectual Property Act No. 36 of 2003. Nevertheless, it has been observed that there are certain structural and operational challenges in the intellectual property ecosystem in the country. Further, although several Ministries and Public Institutions perform complementary roles within the intellectual property ecosystem in addition to the National Intellectual Property Office of Sri Lanka, it has been observed that coordination among these institutions remains limited. Therefore, the need for a National Intellectual Property Policy has been identified to provide a clear strategic direction and to effectively develop and utilize intellectual property in Sri Lanka. Such a policy is expected to give due consideration to international best practices, safeguard national interests, preserve appropriate policy space and address domestic priorities, including the promotion of innovation, knowledge dissemination and public welfare. Taking these matters into consideration, the proposal made by the Minister of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Co-operative Development to formulate a comprehensive National Intellectual Property Policy for Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Development of an Inward Labour Migration Policy for Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although the main focus of the country has been on the management of outbound labour migration, there are now demands for skilled, semi-skilled and specialized foreign workers in certain sectors of the country’s economy. Currently, the regulation of inward labour migration in the country is carried out through multiple administrative procedures implemented by several institutions. The need for formal regulation has been identified by entering information on inward labour migration into a centralized information system. Taking into consideration the said matters, it has been proposed to formulate an Inward Labour Migration Policy for Sri Lanka. The proposed policy will establish a coordinated and transparent national framework to regulate the admission, employment, monitoring and protection of foreign workers coming to Sri Lanka for employment purposes. It will also ensure that the opportunities of Sri Lankan workers are protected. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to introduce an Inward Labour Migration Policy for Sri Lanka and to appoint a Steering Committee chaired by the Secretary to the Ministry of Labour to prepare the draft policy for the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the National Regulatory Reform Council to strengthen Regulatory Governance for Small and Medium Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka’s regulatory environment plays a pivotal role in shaping growth of private sector, influencing investment decisions and enhancing overall business competitiveness. Although the country’s economic fundamentals are strong, it has been observed that the existing regulatory constraints disproportionately affect Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and have also had adverse effects on Sri Lanka’s attractiveness as an investment destination. Taking into account these matters, the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank, has conducted a comprehensive assessment of Sri Lanka’s regulatory framework and, following extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders, has developed the National Regulatory Reform Action Plan and its implementation mechanism. The said Action Plan has put forward a set of practical and actionable recommendations, which have been prioritized and sequenced across short-term, medium-term and long- term horizons. Further, it has also been proposed to establish a National Regulatory Reform Council as the central institutional mechanism for guiding and overseeing the implementation of the said Action Plan. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to establish the said Council under the Chairmanship of the Hon. President and to designate Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development as its Secretariat, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Technical Cooperation Project to enhance the dairy production in the Dry Zone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A Technical Cooperation Project to enhance dairy production in the dry zone is planned to be implemented for a period of 03 years under a financial grant of Rs. 300 million from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). Through the said project, it is expected to achieve the objectives of designing  training and educational programmes, introducing appropriate techniques, strengthening fodder production and supply, improving hygienic milk production and usage, targeting dairy farming entrepreneurs producing 20 to 100 litres of milk per day in the Northern, Eastern, North Central and North Western provinces. Under the project, 02 Districts will be selected from each of the 04 relevant Provinces, and 03 Veterinary Ranges within those Districts will be selected, and it has been planned to establish 24 model farms in those 04 Provinces, with 03 model farms in each of those Veterinary Range.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to implement the Technical Cooperation Project for the Development of Dairy Production in the Dry Zone as proposed, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Membership of the AIA Group Supervisory College by the Insurance Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (IRCSL)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - As one step of the Action Plan to improve the effectiveness of Anti Money Laundering/Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) requirement, action has to be taken by the Insurance Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka to establish a mechanism to share information with foreign counterparts. Accordingly, the IRCSL has planned to obtain the membership of the AIA Group Supervisory College, which is headed by the Insurance Authority of Hong Kong and established to ensure effective cooperation and coordination among insurance supervisory authorities in the Asian region. In order to obtain the said membership, the IRCSL is required to enter into a Coordination Agreement with the Insurance Authority of Hong Kong. The said Agreement will enable the IRCSL to effectively exchange supervisory information with other insurance regulatory/supervisory bodies that have obtained the signatory status of the AIA Group Supervisory College. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development for the Insurance Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka to enter into a Coordination Agreement with the Insurance Authority of Hong Kong to obtain the membership of the AIA Group Supervisory College, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Collaboration Agreement for the University of Jaffna to join the Project for Global Health Research Group on Violence against Women and Children
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A Project of the Global Health Research Group on Violence against Women and Children is implemented with a financial assistance of Rs.173.92 million from the National Institute for Health and Care Research of the United Kingdom. A Collaboration Agreement is to be signed between the University of Jaffna, Sri Lanka and 11 foreign institutions including the University of Birmingham of the United Kingdom to implement the said project. The project will integrate sustainable and better-trained Survivor Panels (Community Engagement and Involvement Groups) into the local health system. It is expected through the project to strengthen the response to violence against women and children, assess the health issues associated with violence against women and children, evaluate its economic and social impacts, identify effective prevention and intervention strategies, and facilitate knowledge exchange and capacity building among institutions. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister, in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, for the University of Jaffna, Sri Lanka to sign the Collaboration Agreement with other relevant parties for the implementation of the said project for a period of 04 years, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement process to select a suitable service provider for the Security Features and Security Features Management System of the Excise Department of Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-11 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Legal provisions relating to affixing security features on liquor products have been introduced by the Excise (Amendment) Act No.26 of 2018. Accordingly, by the Excise Notification No.10/2021 published in the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No.2249/50 dated 2021-10-16, it became mandatory to affix security features on imported foreign liquor, locally manufactured foreign liquor, and local liquor with effect 2021-01-03. The contract period of the company currently entrusted with the printing of security features is scheduled to expire on 2027-01-01. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to implement the procurement process to select a suitable service provider for a period of 5 years to provide the necessary security features and system management services for the relevant data system using the single-stage two‑envelope bidding procedure under the international competitive bidding procedure, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the financial penalties to offences specified under the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-11 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - By the Cabinet decision dated 2025-09-03, policy approval has been granted to amend the fines that can be imposed by the courts for the offences specified in the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956, in a manner that is compatible with the present circumstances. As per the said approval, the Legal Draftsman has prepared a Bill in all the three languages, incorporating provisions to increase the financial penalties specified in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20(A)(3) of the Act from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.100,000/-, and the clearance of the Attorney General has also been received for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to publish the Bill incorporating the said amendments in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the Animals Act, No.29 of 1958
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-11 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - By the Cabinet decision dated 2025-12-01, policy approval has been granted to amend the Interpretation Clause of the Animals Act No.29 of 1958 by including pig, goat and sheep in the definition of 'animal' in addition to 'neat cattle' and 'buffalo'. As per the said approval, an Amendment Bill has been prepared in all the three languages ​​by the Legal Draftsman, and the clearance of the Attorney General has also been received for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to publish the said Amendment Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendments to the State Mortgage and Investment Bank Law No.13 of 1975
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-11 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The State Mortgage and Investment Bank, which came into operation on        1979-01-01, was established by the State Mortgage and Investment Bank Law, No.13 of 1975, with the amalgamation of the Ceylon Mortgage Bank and the Agricultural and Industrial Credit Corporation. Due to certain limitations of the current Act, it has not been possible to achieve the desired goals and maintain the expected profits of the Bank. Therefore, the need to amend the Act has been identified to suit the current business environment and to achieve the desired goals and objectives. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President, in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the said Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of 865,000 Vials of Meropenem Injection 1g vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-11 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-10-21 to award the contract for the supply of 1,900,000 vials of 1 gram Meropenem vaccine, used to treat severe bacterial infections, to United Biotech (Pvt) Ltd., India. Taking into account the increasing demand, a request has been submitted by the Medical Supplies Division for the supply of another 45.53% of the original order quantity, equivalent to 865,000 vials. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the procurement for the repeat order of 865,000 vials of 1 gram Meropenem vaccine at the original order price of US$ 1.05 per vial to the previous supplier, United Biotech (Pvt) Ltd., India (Manufacturer: United Biotech (P) Limited, India), for a total cost and freight cost of US$ 908,250, based on the recommendation of the Standing High Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.
